abstract: We report the case of an extremely large giant neck teratoma diagnosed on routine sonogram and confirmed by 3-D and 4-D sonography and MRI in a 19-year-old primigravida at 18 weeks. Rapid growth, polyhydramnios, premature contractions and premature rupture of membranes necessitated delivery at 28 weeks. Under general anesthesia, with a multidisciplinary team attendant, efforts by the otolaryngologist to establish an airway during an EXIT (ex utero intrapartum treatment) procedure failed as did subsequent attempts by the neonatologist, leading to an early neonatal death. Although a team approach will increase the likelihood of success in securing the airway during EXIT procedures, it cannot be a guarantor in cases of giant neck teratoma.
abstract_ja: 18週の初産婦で、日常の超音波検査で発見され、3D・4D超音波およびMRIで確認された極めて巨大な頸部奇形腫の症例を報告する。急速な増大、羊水過多、早産陣痛および前期破水のため、28週で分娩とした。全身麻酔下で多職種チームのもとEXIT(ex utero intrapartum treatment)手技を行ったが、耳鼻咽喉科医による気道確保は失敗し、その後の新生児科医による試みも成功せず、早期の新生児死亡に至った。EXIT手技において多職種によるチームアプローチは気道確保の成功の可能性を高めるが、巨大頸部奇形腫の症例では成功を保証するものではない。
